title: Bellows return calibration
outcome: Return a bellows gauge to zero after the same standard release, with a diagnosis that can select a remedy without damaging the apparatus.
facts: F1 This untouched heldout case is wholly synthetic.
F2 At z=0,t=0,l=0,o=1: spring s=1 gives signed residual r=1; stronger spring s=2 gives r=2.
F3 Stronger return force is the preferred remedy; increased residual is the anomaly.
F4 Air-lock and backlash maps both fit F2. No true mechanism is stipulated, and real omitted mechanisms remain unknown.
resources: Reversible vent plug z=0 closed or 1 open
Timer t=0 immediate or 1 standardized wait
Reference-loading step l=0 absent or 1 present
constraints: No purchased pressure sensor or destructive disassembly
Hold standard release procedure and zero-return outcome fixed
At most two finite probe cards
Model replay does not establish physical truth
archive: O1 Repeat weak-versus-strong spring at reference F2.
O2 Add an even stronger spring, unavailable and unspecified.
O3 Wait longer without predeclared rival predictions or matched comparison.
O4 Repeat signed residual at the existing reference.
named_dependency: Stronger spring as the sole route to zero return
